                    ### Question
                    Where is the abnormal impulse generated, if in the electrocardiogram we observe an inverted P wave, but the QRS complex and the T wave are normal ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Sinoauricular node.
opb. Atrioventricular node.
opc. Make of His.
opd. Purkinje system.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the context of an electrocardiogram showing an inverted P wave with normal QRS complex and T wave, the abnormal impulse is likely generated near the atrioventricular (AV) node. This is because an inverted P wave suggests retrograde atrial conduction, indicating that the impulse originates from a location other than the sinoatrial node, typically near the AV node. The normal QRS complex and T wave imply that ventricular depolarization and repolarization are unaffected, supporting the conclusion that the impulse is not originating from the ventricles or Purkinje system. The retrieved evidence path mentioning the structure of the atrioventricular node aligns with this reasoning, as it is relevant to the location where such impulses can originate, confirming the consensus that the AV node is the most likely source of the abnormal impulse.
